title: Pillar 11 enforcement + anomaly detection — alert rule files, Telegram bridge, calibrated baseline; live engine evaluation deferred (Option 4)

scope_notes.reduced_scope_disposition: W3 ran under Option 4 reduced scope after a halt-and-surface during bucket 1's alert-engine pre-flight. The plan §W3 (line 197 of design doc, line 237 of plan doc) presumed 'Prometheus Alertmanager or equivalent already running'; that presumption did not hold. Pre-flight evidence: no prometheus/alertmanager/vmalert/grafana-agent binary on PATH or in ~/.local/bin, no prometheus*.yml or alertmanager*.yml config in ~/.config or /etc, no systemd user units for any alert engine, no Docker/Podman runtime, port 9090 occupied by Cockpit (system-management UI, identified via GET / returning Cockpit login HTML and GET /api/v1/status/buildinfo returning the same Cockpit HTML rather than Prometheus JSON). The aho-otel-collector config lists only file + otlp/jaeger exporters — no prometheus, prometheusremotewrite, or alertmanager exporter, so the collector has no path to feed any rule engine even if one existed. Halt was surfaced to Kyle with four forks: stand up Prometheus locally (scope expansion, deferred), use a different engine (no preference declared), defer W3 entirely (Pillar 11 stays unmonitored), or reduce W3 scope (chosen). Reduced scope: rule files, bridge code, calibration, export copy land; bucket 2 (secrets verification) and bucket 5 (synthetic alert delivery test) defer to a later iteration that selects an engine. The framing throughout is 'deliberate deferral, not failure' — engine selection is a non-trivial design decision that should not be silently absorbed into a 4-hour workstream brief, and standing up Prometheus on a workstation is throwaway work given the future-state architecture places metrics infrastructure in Tier 3 managed services.
scope_notes.plan_inconsistency_rule_3: Plan §W3 row 3 specifies expression `rate(claude_code_api_error[5m]) > 1` with parenthetical `(>5 in 5m)`. The two characterisations are inconsistent: rate > 1 ≈ >300 events in 5m, not 5; >5 in 5m would be `increase(...[5m]) > 5`. Per W3 brief instruction 'match plan table exactly — do not adjust thresholds for feel,' the shipped rule uses the formal expression verbatim. Both interpretations are documented in alerts/anomaly-rules.yaml comment, in pillar-11-monitoring-notes.md §Plan inconsistencies item 1, and in export/claude-otel-reference-pack/alerts/README.md §Calibration. Awaiting Kyle/Gemini disposition on which interpretation the plan author intended.
scope_notes.plan_inconsistency_rule_5: Plan §W3 row 5 references metric `claude_code_tool_result_duration_ms_bucket` (Prometheus-style histogram bucket series). Survey of all metric names in ~/.local/share/aho/metrics/metrics.jsonl produced this complete enumeration: claude_code.{active_time.total, cost.usage, token.usage, session.count, lines_of_code.count, code_edit_tool.decision}. No `tool_result.duration_ms` histogram. The duration value lives only as a `duration_ms` attribute on the `claude_code.tool_result` log event. Rule 5's metric reference is therefore aspirational against current Claude Code emission (version 2.1.123 per resource attrs). The bucket-6 calibration sidesteps this by computing p99 from the event attribute (truth source) rather than the non-existent histogram, so the substituted threshold value is honest, but the rule expression is not falsifiable until a metric source is supplied. Three resolution options at engine wire-up time documented in alerts/anomaly-rules.yaml rule-5 comment + pillar-11-monitoring-notes.md §Plan inconsistencies item 2.
scope_notes.calibration_window_honesty: Plan §W3 bucket 6 prescribed 'p99 over W1 + W2 sessions worth of metrics.jsonl data.' Survey found no W1 records in the on-disk logs.jsonl — earliest record is 2026-04-30 17:35 UTC, which postdates W1 close. The OTel file exporter wasn't yet writing during W1. The calibration is W2-only in practice (21 samples, 2026-04-30 17:35 → 2026-05-01 03:40 UTC). 21 samples is thin for a p99 estimate; the linear-interpolation p99 (803.6 ms) is heavily influenced by the single longest observation (max=927). Threshold = 804 × 3 = 2411 ms substituted into rule 5. Comparison run with W3 included (n=93) yielded p99=4748, threshold=14244 — documented but not shipped, since the brief specified W1+W2. Re-runnability via probes/w3_baseline_calibration.py preserved.
scope_notes.metric_naming_assumption: Rule expressions assume bare-name Claude Code metrics in Prometheus form (e.g. `claude_code_commit_count`, no `_total` suffix). The OTel-to-Prometheus translation depends on the eventual exporter version and config; older Prometheus exporters appended `_total` to monotonic counter sums; newer/configurable ones may not. Both rule files and the export pack README flag this as a wire-up-time fix-up. Not falsifiable today since no exporter exists.
scope_notes.event_log_integration_choice: event_log_append() delegates to existing aho.logger.log_event() rather than writing a new schema. Rationale: schema consistency with all other aho events; automatic rotation behavior; identical writer used by every other aho subsystem. Cost: alerts share the rotation buffer with all other events. Distinguishable by event_type ∈ {pillar_11_violation, anomaly} and source_agent='aho-alerts-bridge'. Acceptable per design doc §W3 'alert events also append to aho_event_log.jsonl' (same file, not a separate one).
scope_notes.deferred_synthetic_test_carry: Bucket 5's synthetic alert delivery test (probe → counter increment → rule fire → webhook → Telegram → event log, target <60s wall-clock) is registered as a carry-forward, not a W3 failure. The probe shape is documented in pillar-11-monitoring-notes.md §Deferred verification §B5: hand-rolled OpenTelemetry-Python emitter targeting localhost:4317 with delta-temporality counter is the path of least resistance once an engine is selected.
scope_notes.secrets_creation_kyle_only: Pillar 11 forbids agent secret writes. ahomw:telegram_alerts_bot_token and ahomw:telegram_alerts_chat_id are intentionally not present in the secret store at W3 close. The bridge's _get_alert_creds() raises AlertSecretMissingError on absent secrets — verified by unit test test_get_alert_creds_missing_token / _missing_chat / _empty_string_treated_missing. When Kyle eventually provisions the dedicated @aho_alerts_bot secret pair, the bridge picks them up on next request without code changes.

acceptance_checks.check: Rule-5 baseline calibration computed from W1+W2 metric corpus; threshold substituted into rule file; sentinel TODO_BASELINE_P99_MS removed
acceptance_checks.evidence: Calibration script artifacts/iterations/0.2.16/probes/w3_baseline_calibration.py — re-runnable, accepts custom logs path, workstream filter, and multiplier. Default invocation `python3 probes/w3_baseline_calibration.py` reads ~/.local/share/aho/logs/logs.jsonl, filters resourceLogs where aho.workstream ∈ {W1, W2}, extracts duration_ms attribute from claude_code.tool_result event records, computes percentiles via linear interpolation. Result: 21 samples (all W2; W1 absent from log file — calibration deviated from plan-prescribed window), p99=803.6 ms, threshold=2411 ms (804 × 3, integer-rounded). Substituted into anomaly-rules.yaml rule 5 line 'expr: histogram_quantile(...) > 2411'; verified `grep TODO_BASELINE_P99_MS anomaly-rules.yaml` returns no matches. pass_with_findings rather than pass because: (a) sample size is thin — 21 samples produces high-variance p99 estimate, treated as starting threshold not final; (b) W1 unrecoverable from on-disk files, so canonical 'W1+W2' window collapsed to W2-only in practice; (c) the rule's referenced metric does not exist in Claude Code emission — calibrated value is honest but threshold is unfalsifiable until a metric source is supplied. Findings (a)-(c) documented in pillar-11-monitoring-notes.md §Baseline calibration and §Plan inconsistencies item 2.

carry_forward_candidates.title: Bridge live wire-up
carry_forward_candidates.detail: Once engine is selected: define webhook receiver in engine config pointing at http://127.0.0.1:9095/, create ~/.config/systemd/user/aho-alerts-bridge.service running `python -m aho.alerts.telegram_alerts --serve`, ensure G071 daemon-restart hook runs after any src/aho/alerts/ edit. The BridgeHandler implementation already maps every typed exception to the correct HTTP status code (400/500/502/503) so engine retry semantics are predictable.
